partialCapture.note:
Neither the 456-frame sweep nor the 12-theme sweep was regenerated. Frames added or refreshed here were captured against the same guards (assertFramePaints) but only in the two brand themes, and the live-app frames came from the real Electron window rather than Storybook. The spacing round REFRESHED the five chat-tool-rows surfaces because the row pitch changed under them, and added two: `spacing-uniformity` reproduces the three runs the operator screenshotted, `turn-boundary` shows the hierarchy that survives the tightening. `narrow` and `working-labels` are now captured in a viewport sized to their content — at 1280x900 they were mostly empty ground and crossed the uniformity ceiling once the rows tightened. REMEDIATION ROUND 1: all seven chat-tool-rows surfaces were refreshed again, because the name/summary gutter, the running row's live clock, the sr-only outcome text and the summary fallback all changed what they show. REMEDIATION ROUND 2: `real-conversation-tool-rows` was RE-CAPTURED and is no longer stale. It now shows 38 real tool rows with 0 blank object columns on a 20px pitch, rendered by the shipped reducer and the shipped CanonicalTranscript over real /history pages paged oldest-first in 20-entry pages (the cross-page condition the blank-summary defect needed). Electron is not required for this surface — the desktop API answers a plain bearer request. The reading was proven falsifiable by running the SAME harness with the reducer starved: stripping tool_calls alone still yields 0 blanks (the output fallback carries it), stripping tool_calls AND output yields 53 of 53 blank, reproducing the original defect from the current head. DIFF BODY: two surfaces were ADDED — the `write`/`edit` row's expansion now paints the result's own unified diff instead of its arguments JSON — and four frames were taken for them in the two brand palettes (`chat-tool-rows--diff-body` at 1280x2110 and `chat-tool-rows--diff-body-narrow` at 560x1380). The four Storybook frames are committed under `write-edit-diff/` rather than under the story-id directory the capturer derives (`chat-tool-rows/<leaf>`), following the `tool-rows/` precedent, so that the frames sit beside the spec and README that explain them; a re-capture writes them back to `chat-tool-rows/`. `surfaces` counts the two new STORIES entries. The 12-theme sweep was NOT regenerated. A sixth frame set is declared in `supplementary` below: three real durable diff rows in one conversation (197, 58 and 14 diff lines — the first two longer than the 40-line display cap, so two overflow markers and one body shown whole) rendered by the SHIPPED reducer and transcript over real transcript.jsonl rows. The story proves the component; that one proves the wire payload reaches pixels. DIFF BODY, REMEDIATION ROUND 1: the same two Storybook surfaces were refreshed again and a THIRD was added, because the body now paints each line whole in its kind's ink instead of tinting only the leading marker (the terminal's loop is the authority; its docstring promises the other thing), and because the cap's `… N more diff lines` marker is now pinned to the well's foot with `sticky -bottom-3 pb-3 -mb-3` — it used to scroll out of view in exactly the wrapped-at-cap case it exists for. The new surface, `chat-tool-rows--diff-body-narrow-wrapped-cap` at 560x830, is the frame that shows the marker visible at rest; `frames` moves 478 -> 480 for its two palettes, and it is the only frame count that changed. The `real-durable-diff-rows` pair was RE-CAPTURED in the same round for the same reason (on the same real conversation, same three diffs of 197, 58 and 14 lines) and carries the identical marker arithmetic. It was captured from the committed source, not from a dirty tree: this partial run's `head`, `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` name the commit whose pixels these are. The neighbour `tool-rows/*` frames were NOT re-captured — they are from the August head and do not reproduce pixel-exactly on this one (a uniform 11px shift with identical internal geometry, across three stories of different content), which the write-edit-diff README records so nobody reads it as a regression from this change. REBASE RE-PIN, no frame re-captured: the three provenance fields above name the rebased equivalents (`aa5bbbf24` -> `fdccf36f4`, `1cf21bc6` -> `0b9ee794`, `dd0fa890` -> `4e60e49a`) of the commits these pixels were taken at, because the branch was replayed onto `104b0321a` (the chat diff body, #114) after review round 4. #114 touches no file any surface this branch captured: its renderer changes are all under `features/chat/`, and the only file both sides edited is `scripts/capture-evidence.mjs`, where the two STORIES additions auto-merged. So a re-capture would re-take pixels that cannot differ, and the fields move only because the rebased code head carries #114's own src/scripts content. REBASE RE-PIN, round 6, and the first re-render at a rebased head: the branch was replayed onto `1f241ba87` (the 0.17.1 release bump, on top of #111, the backend-composed notification toasts). The 14 frames named above were RE-RENDERED through this pipeline at the rebased head (`pnpm storybook` plus `node scripts/capture-evidence.mjs --only=updatenotification --themes=localOperatorDark,localOperatorLight`) and came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed set (sha256 of all 24 files in this directory unchanged before and after), so the run rewrote no frame and the three provenance fields plus the four `partialCapture` head/time fields now name the head it really ran at, `61f3ed22e`, and that head's own `src` and `scripts` trees. #111 touches no file any surface here renders: its changes are `src/main/desktop-notifier.ts`, `src/main/desktop-ipc.ts`, `src/main/backend/backend-service.ts`, `src/main/index.ts`, the two `src/shared/desktop-*contract.ts` schemas and two new `scripts/` files, and nothing under `src/renderer/` - the renderer tree is byte-identical across the replay (`git diff 70fd947c6 61f3ed22e -- src/renderer` is empty). Its `frontend.update` frame is the session stream's own delta, not an app update, so it neither composes nor announces anything this panel shows. The only file both sides edited is `package.json`, where the two `test:desktop` additions (upstream's `scripts/desktop-notifier.test.mjs` and this branch's `scripts/update-robustness.test.mjs`) were unioned. The ten non-brand-theme `update-available` frames were NOT re-taken and still carry the August sweep.

THIS BRANCH (fix/tool-row-args-recovery) ON TOP OF THAT: the tool row's object column is recovered from a mid-turn snapshot's seed, which carries settling frames and no arguments — so rows that read `exit code: 0`, `Edited <path>`, `result: None` or a bare line number now name the call. The eight `chat-tool-rows--*` surfaces were refreshed in the two brand themes, `states` gained a composing row and `joined-mid-turn` a silent call and a truncated stand-in row, and every line that reaches the object column from the RESULT rather than from the call now carries a leading `…` so a column that is normally a command cannot be misread as one. A sweep also no longer deletes non-frame files: it clears the `.webp` frames it can retake and keeps the READMEs, the hand-taken PNG pairs and `tui-parity/OPERATOR-TUI-REFERENCE.md` — 123 committed files that a sweep used to take with the frames, with this gate green over the loss. Six sets are now declared: the two above, this branch's `tool-rows-baseline` (the before/after pair, which needs an older source tree), `chat-tool-rows/spacing-uniformity`, `chat-tool-rows/real-conversation-tool-rows`, `transcript-images/real-conversation-images` and `onboarding-onboardingmodal/radient-sign-in` (its story was removed with the Tailwind v4 landing, and the dead STORIES entry made every full sweep abort before this fix). `docs/evidence/tool-rows` was renamed to `chat-tool-rows` because the capturer derives a surface directory from the story title slug, and the title gained a `Chat/` prefix after the set was first written.

MERGE UP TO `origin/main` (#114, #113, #111, #107): the resolution re-captured, at the merged head, the eight `chat-tool-rows--*` story surfaces, the six `chat-trace--*` ones and the three `write-edit-diff/diff-body*` ones (two byte-identical to main's; the wide pair replaced in place because this branch's row spellings changed it, and the derived copies under `chat-tool-rows/` deleted rather than left beside them). Three of the `chat-trace` surfaces came back at 900px on the first attempt, because `capture-evidence` sizes a frame with `Math.max(documentElement.scrollHeight, declared)` and the transcript has been its own scroll container since #101: the document then reports the viewport, the max collapses to the declared 900 and the frame clips the conversation - `conversation-reasoning-open` lost 2,427px including two of the three open reasoning panels it exists to evidence. They now declare their content heights (1308 / 1409 / 3327) and were re-captured at them, which is what `refreshedStories` above describes.

supplementary.why: The claims are a real pointer hover and a click that stages a draft. Storybook can force the revealed class but not produce the hover, and a staged draft is store state a fixture would have to fake, so these are captured from the running app against an isolated seeded backend instead. The sidebar has no story, so re-running the sweep cannot re-derive them; docs/evidence/sidebar-new-chat/README.md carries the re-capture procedure.

supplementary.source: headless Chrome over CDP, driven by `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs`: the shipped `applyHistoryPage` reducer and the shipped `CanonicalTranscript` over a real durable history page read from one real session's `transcript.jsonl` in the local store (`--session` and `--anchor` are required arguments; the id is deliberately not committed)
supplementary.why: The story renders a TranscriptRecord this repository built, so it proves the component. This set starts one layer earlier, at the bytes `/v1/desktop/sessions/{id}/history` serves — the stored rows, serialised verbatim by `read_transcript_page` — and runs them through the shipped reducer, which is what proves the payload reaches pixels: the durable row's own encoding, the extraction of `provider_payload.details.diff`, the identity gate and the args-drop rule. It cannot be re-derived by the sweep, and the payload itself is deliberately NOT committed: the harness writes it to a temp file and deletes it. Re-run with `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs --session=<id> --anchor=<row id>` (see docs/evidence/write-edit-diff/README.md).
